title: Perimeter
summary: Perimeter is the total distance around a shape — the sum of all its sides. Explore how to measure around polygons, find missing sides, and when perimeter shows up in real life.

compareCandidate.label: Perimeter vs. area
compareCandidate.description: Perimeter walks AROUND the shape (a distance); area tiles the INSIDE (a surface). The same perimeter can surround very different areas.

plainLanguageExplanation: Perimeter is the total distance around a shape — imagine walking along its edge until you return to your start. Add up the lengths of every side to find it. For a triangle with sides 3, 4, and 5, the perimeter is 3 + 4 + 5 = 12. A rectangle has two lengths and two widths, so its perimeter is 2 × length + 2 × width. If you know the perimeter and all but one side, subtract to find the missing one. Fencing a yard, framing a picture, and edging a garden are all perimeter jobs.

keyFacts.label: Missing side
keyFacts.value: Subtract known sides from the total

whyItMatters: Whenever something wraps around the edge of a shape — a fence, a frame, a border — the amount you need is the perimeter. It is the practical measurement of outlines.
didYouKnow: 'Perimeter' comes from Greek — 'peri' means around and 'metron' means measure. So perimeter literally means 'measuring around' the outside.
compareReason: Perimeter and area are the classic pair students mix up — comparing around vs. inside makes each one unforgettable.
